hints.title: Tracking Seen Integers
hints.text: Maintain occurrences of elements as both permutations are traversed synchronously.

hints.title: Duplicate Occurrence Means Common Element
hints.text: When an integer's occurrence reaches two, it has appeared in both prefixes and increases the common count.

hints.title: Running Prefix Counter
hints.text: At each step, update counts for A[i] and B[i], check if either reached frequency two, and record current count.

hints.title: Frequency-Based Prefix Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def findThePrefixCommonArray(self, A: list[int], B: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        n = len(A)
        count = [0] * (n + 1)
        common = 0
        ans = []
        for x, y in zip(A, B):
            count[x] += 1
            if count[x] == 2:
                common += 1
            count[y] += 1
            if count[y] == 2:
                common += 1
            ans.append(common)
        return ans
```

variables: n: length of permutations A and B
complexity.notes: Single pass counting element frequencies up to n.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Intersecting prefix sets at every position takes O(n^2) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Maintains a running count when element frequency reaches two.
